title: Azul 2026 AI Vulnerability Gap Report: 85% of Organisations Running Java Have Had an Incident, Suspected Incident or Near Miss Due to Slow Patching
headline: Azul 2026 AI Vulnerability Gap Report on Patching and AI Attackers
summary: A survey of 300 security leaders by Azul and Censuswide reveals that 85% of organisations running Java have experienced an incident or near miss due to slow patching. The report highlights that AI-powered attack tools have accelerated exploitation timelines, creating a widening gap between how fast attackers can build exploits and how long enterprises take to test and deploy patches. Internal constraints such as extensive pre-deployment testing and limited runtime visibility continue to impede rapid remediation.
why_it_matters: Organisations must reassess their vulnerability management and patching timelines to account for AI-equipped attackers who can build exploits faster than traditional enterprise testing cycles allow.

quotes.text: The report finds that 85% of organisations have already experienced an incident or near miss attributable to slow patching, including 55% who report a confirmed incident and 53% who report a near miss, as AI shrinks the time attackers need to exploit newly disclosed vulnerabilities.
Agentic AI has collapsed the margin defenders depend on, and most enterprises are still running patch processes built for a much slower adversary

classification.significance_reason: Provides empirical data on enterprise vulnerability management and AI-driven exploitation timelines, though it is primarily vendor-sponsored research focused on US security leaders.
